// Every subtest here is the prohibited (*qt.C).Run shape written so that the
// callback is not an inline func(*qt.C) literal. A rule that only inspects the
// second argument's literal signature reports none of them.
package fixture

import (
	"testing"

	qt "github.com/frankban/quicktest"
)

type holder struct {
	checker *qt.C
}

type carrier struct{}

func (carrier) sub(c *qt.C) {
	c.Assert(1, qt.Equals, 1)
}

func declared(c *qt.C) {
	c.Assert(2, qt.Equals, 2)
}

func TestIndirectSubtests(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)

	assigned := func(c *qt.C) {
		c.Assert(3, qt.Equals, 3)
	}

	c.Run("callback declared at file scope", declared)
	c.Run("callback assigned to a variable", assigned)
	c.Run("callback this package cannot resolve without types", carrier{}.sub)

	outer := qt.New(t)
	outer.Run("receiver is not named c", declared)

	qt.New(t).Run("receiver is not an identifier at all", declared)
}

func TestReceiverReachedThroughAField(t *testing.T) {
	h := holder{checker: qt.New(t)}

	// The receiver is a selector this package cannot resolve; the callback is
	// what identifies the shape.
	h.checker.Run("named callback on an unresolvable receiver", declared)
}
